cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Ask Around the Missing Detail
cards.instruction: Find one hidden fact by asking about everything surrounding it and never naming it directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Whose coat needed the second cup of tea while I was out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Coats don't drink tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. True. Who was keeping that one warm from the inside?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're asking who visited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still on the cup. Did its owner take sugar?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking whether you'd pass the salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request is under consideration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. Approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to my garage sale. Your offer to browse is accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my garage. You're helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're doing very well under my supervision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Take five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whose coat needed the second cup of tea while I was out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Coats don't drink tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: True. Who was keeping that one warm from the inside?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're asking who visited.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still on the cup. Did its owner take sugar?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What time did the kitchen light go off after the extra dinner plate was used?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask who came over?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to understand the timetable first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We ate late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then which bus carried the timetable's missing person home?

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Will you help me tidy the committee cupboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sure. Where do we start?

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to tidy, not overthrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm asking again, now you can see what we've been storing.

cards.title: Make the Second Step First
cards.instruction: Get them to accept a small consequence that makes the larger risky action feel already underway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Pay the climbing-course deposit before we discuss the cliff.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to climb.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. It's refundable only if we attend the first lesson.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So paying makes not climbing harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A small commitment can do the worrying for us.

cards.title: Let the Callback Claim Credit
cards.instruction: Get recognition by returning to an early overlooked contribution when its importance becomes undeniable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Remember my suggestion to put the spare key under the flowerpot?

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. Good idea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say whose idea while you lift it. The pot can't accept all the credit.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Choose the overseas job or our shared shop. Then we'll know what 'we'll build something' meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before the offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Yes. This choice gives the old sentence its ending.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making a job sound like a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking whether your promise has room for the shop without you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking whether you'd pass the salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request is under consideration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. Approved.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Take five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Choose the overseas job or our shared shop. Then we'll know what 'we'll build something' meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said that before the offer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. This choice gives the old sentence its ending.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making a job sound like a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking whether your promise has room for the shop without you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep my spare key or return it. Either choice explains last week's 'take some space.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant a quiet evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then keeping it can mean the evening ended.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And returning it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would make that evening the beginning of something neither of us named.
